ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Basic, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Bash.cs:24-27) == cost 2 / ATTACK / BASIC / ANY_ENEMY. No keywords, no tags (Bash carries no CardTag.Strike, and the sim leaves `tags` empty).

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(8m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new PowerVar<VulnerablePower>(2m)` (Bash.cs:18-22) == `_damage = 8`, `_vulnerable = 2`. Damage props are Move without Unpowered -> powered on both sides (`DamageProps.CARD`, valueprops.py:34). `_vulnerable` is first in `Card._MAGIC_ATTRS` (cards/base.py:185-189) so `magic_number` returns 2, matching the game's second printed var.

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The card's own `if not target.is_gone:` is DELETED and PowerCmd.apply now carries the WHOLE of `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-322): `cmds.can_receive_powers` is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)`, and `Creature.is_removed_from_combat` (creatures.py) is `is_gone and not retained_after_death` -- the sim's expression of `CombatState == null`, since it never drops a corpse from `enemies` (conformance addresses enemies by index). The two edits are a MATCHED PAIR: round 6 had wired only the ShouldAllowHitting half here, so deleting the card guard on its own would have powered the ordinary corpse that CreatureCmd.cs:523-531 removes. Pinned by test/test_can_receive_powers.py -- ordinary corpse refused, removal-vetoed corpse powered, mid-revival corpse still refused. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable the entry proposed -- a Vicious draw off a retained corpse -- is not reachable in the sim's SHIPPED content, and the enumeration is the finding. Every sim producer of a retained corpse also makes it unhittable for as long as it lasts (IllusionPower.cs:95-105, AdaptablePower.cs:68-78 and ReattachPower.cs:74-86 each pair the removal veto with ShouldAllowHitting), the sole exception being a Decimillipede segment killed with every other segment already down -- and that ends the combat, so PowerCmd.Apply's own IsEnding guard (PowerCmd.cs:69-72) swallows it first. The game's third case, PainfulStabsPower.cs:29-32 on Test Subject phase 2, retains WITHOUT vetoing hits and the sim's PainfulStabsPower omits that override; recorded here rather than fixed, because it is not this entry's line. The code is now the source's shape either way.  The text it replaced read: The damage, the ordering (damage BEFORE the debuff) and both amounts are faithful. The divergence is the sim's extra liveness guard: `if not target.is_gone: PowerCmd.apply(..., VulnerablePower, ...)` (bash.py:40-41). C# applies the Vulnerable UNCONDITIONALLY (`PowerCmd.Apply<VulnerablePower>(choiceContext, cardPlay.Target, ...)`, Bash.cs:35) and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose own doc comment says the quiet part out loud: "a creature is not hittable if it's dead, but dead creatures CAN still have powers applied to them" -- it refuses only when `CombatState == null` (the corpse was REMOVED) or `Hook.ShouldAllowHitting` says no. For an ordinary monster the two agree, because `CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `await Kill(killedCreatures)` before returning (CreatureCmd.cs:409) and `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition` removes the creature from combat at CreatureCmd.cs:523-525, nulling its CombatState before Bash's next statement. They DIVERGE for a corpse whose removal was vetoed: `Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` (CreatureCmd.cs:508) can return false, the sim models exactly that as `target.retained_after_death = not hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death(target)` (cmds.py:100-104, with ReattachPower/Decimillipede named as the case), and `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46), so the sim SKIPS a creature C# still powers. Observable via a ported listener: `ViciousPower` draws `Amount` cards on any Vulnerable the owner applies, with no liveness test on the target (`ViciousPower.cs:19-26`: `if (!(amount <= 0m) && applier == Owner && power is VulnerablePower)`), and the sim's port is the same shape (powers.py:1569-1598). So: hold Vicious, Bash a retained-corpse enemy to death -- the game draws cards, the sim does not. LIVE: card/vicious, card/bash, ViciousPower and the retained-corpse path (`powers.py:2933-2960` ReattachPower, `combat.py:292,306`) are all ported. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards` enumerates the pool-wide pattern -- 41 sim card classes test liveness, and bash is one of the `if not target.is_gone:` form. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): CreatureCmd.cs, Creature.cs, ViciousPower.cs, cmds.py, creatures.py and powers.py are not hashed by this record. Presentation, folded in: ExtraHoverTips -> HoverTipFactory.FromPower<VulnerablePower> (Bash.cs:16) is hover-tip wiring.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` + `DynamicVars.Vulnerable.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Bash.cs:40-41) == `_damage += 2` (8 -> 10) and `_vulnerable += 1` (2 -> 3). Both upgraded numbers checked, not just the base pair. Downgrade-safe; `card_probes.py downgrade` does not list bash.

guards.rationale: AnyEnemy cards always resolve a target; `ctx.resolve_target(target_idx)` is the sim's equivalent contract.

guards.what: the Vulnerable is applied with `applier = Owner.Creature` and `cardSource = this` (Bash.cs:35)
guards.rationale: The sim passes `applier=ctx.player`, which is what ViciousPower's `applier == Owner` test needs. The dropped `cardSource` argument on `PowerCmd.apply` is the power_cmd seam's finding, not a card-level one.
